sentences.text: Briefly stated, the case of the prosecution against the accused is that on 23.10.2017 at about 11.30 pm at road no. 56 in front of Anand Vihar bus terminal towards Seemapuri to Ghazipur, Delhi, one person was driving a bus bearing no. UP 81 BT 5911 in a rash and negligent manner and while driving so, he struck against an auto bearing no. DL 1RK 6850 belonging to the complainant Balvinder Singh.

As such, it is alleged that the accused committed an offence under sections 279 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter, "IPC") for which FIR No. 376/2017 was registered at Police Station Madhu Vihar, Delhi.
INVESTIGATION AND APPEARANCE OF ACCUSED 2.

After registration of FIR, the investigating officer (hereinafter 'IO') conducted investigation and on culmination of the investigation, chargesheet against the present accused namely Arvind Singh for the alleged commission of offences u/s 279 IPC was filed.
Ld. Predecessor of this court took cognizance of the offence u/s 279 IPC vide order dated 18.07.2018.

After taking cognizance of the offence, accused appeared before the Court and he was supplied the copy of documents relied upon in the charge sheet in terms of section 207 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter,
"CrPC").
3.

Since prima facie offences against the accused were made out, Ld. Predecessor of this Court vide order dated 30.09.2019 framed notice against accused Arvind Singh for the offence punishable u/s 279 IPC, to Digitally which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

During the trial, prosecution led the following oral and documentary evidence against the accused to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt:
ORAL EVIDENCE PW1 Sh. Deepchand Jain DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE Ex.PW1/A

Mechanical inspection report of the offending bus dated 26.10.2017 ADMITTED DOCUMENTS u/s 294 Cr.P.C.

Ex. P2 DD No. 42 dated 23.10.2017 PP  ISBT of PS Madhu Vihar  Ex. P3 Certificate u/s 65B IEA  Ex. P4
Mechanical inspection report of  vehicle no. DL 1RK 6850 5.

Sh. Deepchand Jain (PW1) in his examination-in-chief deposed that in the year 2017, he was posted as Senior Foreman at UP Roadways, Kaushambi Depot,
Ghaziabad.
On 26.10.2017, he went to PS Madhu Vihar, where he inspected the bus bearing registration number UP 81 BT 5911.

He prepared a report regarding the State vs Arvind Singh on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20421243/
2 inspection dated 26.10.2017 Ex.PW1/A and handed it over to the Investigating Officer (IO).
The witness identified the offending bus in the two photographs of the bus bearing number UP 81 BT 5911, attached with the judicial file Ex.X1 (colly).

5.1.On his cross
- examination by Ld. Counsel for accused
, the witness stated that he does not remember whether he received any notice from the IO regarding the mechanical inspection of the bus bearing number UP 81 BT 5911 due to the lapse of time.
He denied the suggestion that he does not remember because no notice was received.
He also denied the suggestion that he was deposing falsely.

6. During course of trial, complainant/eyewitness Balvinder remained unserved in the present matter even after steps taken through DCP and accordingly he was dropped from the list of witnesses on 09.11.2023.

As the witness PW1 was already examined and formal documents without their contents were already admitted by the accused u/s 294 CrPC hence, this Court by relying upon the order of the Hon'ble Apex Court of India in the matter titled In Re: Speedy Trial of Under Trial Prisoners (dated 22.10.2018), closed prosecution evidence today.
STATEMENT AND DEFENCE OF ACCUSED 7.
Since no incriminating evidence was brought forth by the prosecution, recording of statement of accused u/s 313 CrPC was dispensed with.
Accused chose not to lead evidence in his defence.
ARGUMENTS 8.
I have heard the Ld. APP for the State and Ld. Counsel for the accused.
I have also given my thoughtful consideration to the material available on record.
POINT OF DETERMINATION 9.

After going through the record and considering the material available on record, the only point of determination that is left is whether the Udbhav Digitally by Udbhav Kumar Jain signed Kumar Date:
2025.07.08 Jain 16:54:17 +0530 FIR No. 376/2017 State v. Arvind Singh Page no. 4 of 6 prosecution in the absence of material witness can substantiate its case and prove the guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt.

REASONS FOR DECISION OF THE CASE State vs Arvind Singh on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20421243/
3 10.
The general burden of proof on the prosecution is that of beyond a reasonable doubt.
The presumption of innocence of the accused has to be rebutted by the prosecution by adducing cogent evidence that points towards the guilt of the accused.
The evidence in the present case is to be weighed keeping in view the above legal standards.
11. The complainant/eyewitness failed to appear before the Court even after steps taken through DCP and he was dropped from the list of witnesses.

In the absence of complainant/eyewitness,
identification of accused, commission of offence and his presence on the spot remains doubtful.
It is not the case that the alleged offence was committed behind closed doors, and it is highly unlikely that not even a single person saw the alleged commission of offence.
Other witnesses who were dropped were also not present on the spot on the date of alleged offence.
No public witness was called to support the case of prosecution.
Therefore, non-appearance of complainant/eyewitness and absence of any public witness are factors which makes the story of prosecution unbelievable.
12. Further, PW-1 is the witness subsequent to the alleged incident/offence and he did not see the alleged commission of offence.
As such, even if all the other prosecution witness cited in the list of witnesses were to be examined, the case of the prosecution could not be proved.

13. Furthermore, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in S.L. Goswami (Dr) v. State of M.P.,
(1972) 3 SCC 22 that the accused is entitled to benefit of doubt where the onus of proving the ingredients of the offence Digitally signed by FIR No. 376/2017 State v. Arvind SinghUdbhav Udbhav Page no. 5 of 6 Kumar Jain Kumar Date:
 Jain 2025.07.08  16:54:23  +0530 is not discharged by the prosecution.

sentences.text: In the present case, as already noted above, the prosecution could not discharge the onus of proving the ingredients of offence as the complainant/material witness turned hostile.
Thus, accused Arvind Singh is entitled to benefit of doubt.
CONCLUSION 14.
In view of the above discussion, the accused Arvind Singh is hereby found not guilty.
Accordingly, accused Arvind Singh is hereby acquitted of the offences under section 279 IPC.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
Announced in open court today i.e., 08.07.2025.
